Operated/accessed from Australia ground facilities, designed above Great Barrier Reef. Includes STK simulations, perturbation calculations, launch alternatives, EOL.

Main body mission design: Launch: discusses piggyback, factors, equator, politics, uses Wikipedia "Timeline of spaceflight" as directory [6]. Compares Vega VV18 and Falcon 9 rideshare. Chooses Vega E rocket from Guiana Space Centre. There are errors: says Kourou latitude 45.05°N – that's wrong; Kourou is ~5.2°N. They say "As this is smaller than target inclination, two launch windows per day – ascending/descending node." Actually launch site latitude relative to inclination: if site latitude 5.2 N and target inclination 87.79 or 98? Wait sun-synchronous at 600 km inclination should be ~97.79° (retrograde), not 87.79°. Critical error. They wrote inclination 87.79° required for 600 km SSO. For SSO, inclination >90 for retrograde; at 600 km about 97.8°. Their graph shows 98.5 at 600, but text says 87.7924. They use 87.79° in table. This is inconsistent and major. A near-polar retrograde sun-synchronous orbit should be ~97.8°, not 87.8°. The graph's y-axis values 96.5-99.5, at 600 around 97.8, not 87.7924. The table says 87.79. That is a serious technical error. Also they say "retrograde" in exec but 87.79 is prograde (slightly). Need mention. Also RAAN 27.33° initial indicates launch facility? No argument of perigee/true anomaly due circular; okay. But SSO inclination wrong. "Sun-synchronous orbit inherently experiences significant J2 perturbations as a result of highly polar inclination. This is what allows orbit maintain orientation relative to Sun. For truly sun-synchronous, RAAN must change rate 360 per year (i.e. full rotation); ascending node experiencing 1° east-ward precession every day" 360/year ≈ 0.986°/day, okay. But direction? For SSO, RAAN precesses eastward? Actually sun-synchronous orbits have RAAN precession ~0.9856°/day eastward (same direction as Earth's orbital motion). Okay. "Argument of Latitude" introduced. Good. "If daily images entire reef require swath 250 km; sensor swinging or high altitude; high altitude low resolution 'also desirable' typo should be undesirable. But if sun-synchronous, launch window constrained by local time; not any two per day? Actually for SSO, launch time must target specific RAAN/local time, so only one per day generally? Hmm.

Ground: selects Mt Pleasant Radio Observatory in Tasmania. STK access summary. Average duration table: Mean duration 580.786 sec = 9.68 minutes, not "almost twenty minutes." They claim "satellite will be recording data in descending part of orbit – where satellite is constantly in sunlight." Is descending side always in sunlight for SSO?
